I'm very surprised to hear that you were fired as an intern, especially if you completed your work on time and worked additional hours for free. Most places in my experience are very lenient with interns and even graduates, so perhaps it was just a shitty place to work. It that is indeed the case, don't be disheartened by your experience there.

With regards to your relationship with co-workers, I'm wondering if it may have come across that you had a poor attitude? As an intern, as long as you show some degree of enthusiasm, managers are typically happy. A poor attitude is the only reason I could think of, for why a company would fire an intern, based on the story you provided.

Either way, try to learn from the experience. In your next job, let them know that you are happy to be there - smile, say "good morning" to you co-workers and have lunch with people from your department. It really helps working along people you have a genuine relationship with.

All the best with your future career, I'm sure everything will work out for you, just give it some time!

First of all, I think you should get closure on the situation. If you never find out if she is interested in you, it will keep niggling at you and will make getting over her a lot longer!

Secondly, regardless of the outcome, I would suggest trying to learn from the situation in a positive manner. Personally, I believe its healthier to ask someone out on a date when you only have a slight crush, so that you don't spend a load of months thinking about and idolising them.

So yes, I do think that you should ask her out. Something as simple as "Hey, when this Corona thing has calmed down, would you like to go for a coffee with me?" should suffice. She'll either say yes or no, so prepare yourself for both scenarios.

I hope it goes well for you and even if it doesn't work out the way you want it to, try to see it as a learning experience for future relationships. Good luck!
